title: Session-affinity token prober for SSE/WebSocket with deterministic p95 regression detection
creator: Ava Patel
description: Build a scalable, reproducible load-probing harness that exercises streaming chat paths over both SSE and WebSocket protocols with session affinity and deterministic token pacing. The harness will measure tokens/sec, per-session token arrival latency distributions, and compute rolling p95/p99 for token arrival and final response completion. It must be able to: (1) emulate multi-tenant mixes (short/long sessions, varying token budgets), (2) preserve KV-cache warm/cold scenarios, (3) inject controlled jitter and connection churn, and (4) produce deterministic traces so regressions can be replayed and gated in CI and alerting rules.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run 50k concurrent logical sessions across a distributed driver cluster and sustain 250k tokens/sec total throughput in our staging fleet
End-to-end token arrival p95 is computed per-tenancy and reported to Grafana with 1m and 5m rollups
Regression detector produces a deterministic alert when p95 increases by >20% relative to a baseline window and saves a replay bundle to S3
Supports SSE and WebSocket protocols with identical metrics and can switch behavior via config file
KV-cache-aware scenarios: cold-start, warmed-by-prefix, and mixed-tenancy runs are available as presets
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for session state machine and token pacing. 2) Local harness smoke: 100 concurrent sessions, validate metrics. 3) Staging runs: scale to 10k, 25k, 50k logical sessions while capturing token/sec, p95/p99, error rates. 4) Create baseline runs and store baseline artifacts. 5) Introduce synthetic regressions (artificial kernel slowdown) and verify regression detector fires and replay reproduces the anomaly. 6) Run nightly canary with limited tenants and gate on p95 delta < 10%
implementation_notes: Architecture: coordinator (stateless) + distributed drivers (stateful), drivers simulate clients and push events to runtime endpoints via SSE/WS
Session affinity: drivers attach synthetic tenant headers and maintain a deterministic seed per session to enable exact replay
Token pacing: implement token-production schedule derived from real production token histograms; support exponential and bursty modes
Metrics: emit per-session token-arrival histograms, aggregate tokens/sec, connection churn rate, and error classification (5xx, timeouts, protocol errors)
Regression detection: compare rolling p95 against stored baseline using Hellinger distance + relative delta heuristic before alerting
Storage: replay bundles (session seeds, request payloads, timelines) uploaded to s3://redwood-load-replays/YYYYMMDD/ for investigation
Observability: Grafana dashboard (link below) with per-model and per-region breakdown, and synthetic trace links back to Honeycomb
Cost tradeoffs: pushing to 50k logical sessions will require driver autoscaling and temporary dedicated GPU staging nodes — coordinate with infra to reserve capacity for ramp tests
